page: Vultr vx1-g-48c-192g-2880s is a general-purpose compute instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute line, featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 192.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 4:1 memory-to-core ratio with 4.0 GB per vCPU. The node is provisioned with 2880 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Dedicated hardware accelerators are not included, as the GPU count is zero.

Benchmark measurements position the host strongly across compute and storage-adjacent metrics. The AMD EPYC processors register top-tier performance in Geekbench single-core (2774.0) and multi-core (26519.0) tests, along with top-tier results in Clang software compilation (58196.0) and stress-ng single-core processing (3694.27). CPU instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions (such as AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI, delivering a PassMark encryption score of 62796.71.

Memory and I/O throughput tests indicate strong cache-level responsiveness, reaching 5377.89 GB/sec in 16 KB cached reads, alongside top-tier 256 MB uncached write speeds of 257.22 GB/sec. Uncached large-block read operations register an average score of 162.88 GB/sec, accompanied by an average PassMark memory score of 2089.25. CPU-based LLM inference tests yield top-tier generation rates of 407.62 tokens/sec on 135M models and 50.6 tokens/sec on 7B models, though prompt processing and larger 70B model throughput align with midrange averages.

The dense pairing of 48 dedicated vCPUs, 192 GB of memory, and 2.88 TB of local NVMe storage delivers high compute density on a unified node. This configuration is suited for large software compilation pipelines, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational and non-relational database systems, data compression tasks, and static web serving workloads requiring fast local disk access.
description: Vultr vx1-g-48c-192g-2880s is a general-purpose compute instance configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical AMD EPYC cores at 2.0 GHz, 192.0 GB of memory, and 2880 GB of integrated NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 platform features advanced vector extensions including AVX-512, SHA-NI, and AES encryption acceleration. In synthetic testing, it scores in the top tier for Geekbench multi-core performance (26519.0), software compilation with Clang (58196.0), and uncached large-block memory writes (257.22 GB/sec). Network capabilities include one complimentary public IPv4 address, and the server contains no discrete GPUs. With 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU alongside rapid local NVMe storage, this instance is suited for multi-threaded compilation pipelines, Redis deployments, enterprise databases, and static web serving.
